clue.text: Adversity maiden is getting in exchange for strain

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
taken as written
one thing is given for another when exchanged, so 'in exchange for' gives FOR
a strain is a melody or air

explanation.surface: A young woman is being swapped in return for some stress she is under.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' is only a link joining the definition to the wordplay; the pieces simply line up in clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: Adversity is a state of hardship or bad luck, a synonym.

clue.text: Fashions not quite decent

indicators.note: something not quite whole is missing its final bit, so the word for decent loses its last letter

parts.note: decent, as in proper and seemly, means modest

explanation.surface: Some styles of dress are just a little too revealing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' drops the final T from MODEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Modes are prevailing styles or trends, a synonym of fashions.

clue.text: Romanians undergoing revolution to form a republic

indicators.note: letters undergoing a revolution are overturned and rearranged, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: People of Romania rise up in revolt to set up a republic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'undergoing revolution' looks political but signals that the nine letters of ROMANIANS are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: San Marino is a tiny independent republic inside Italy, an example.

clue.text: Honour determining who gets to wash first?

definitions.meaning: a British order of chivalry awarded as a distinction

definitions.text: determining who gets to wash first?
definitions.meaning: read literally, the phrase describes settling the sequence in which people take turns in the tub

explanation.surface: An award decided by who gets the bathroom first.
explanation.walkthrough: The Order of the Bath is a British order of knighthood; read as plain words it means the sequence of bathers.
explanation.definitionFit: This British order of chivalry is an honour conferred by the monarch, an example.

clue.text: Soldiers drank rum in drinking vessel

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve soldiers

indicators.note: rum here means odd or strange, signalling that the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Troops knocked back rum from a beer mug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the drink but is the old British adjective for strange, the anagram signal turning DRANK into NKARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A tankard is a tall beer mug, an example of a drinking vessel.

clue.text: Presidential initiative that follows a reshuffle

definitions.meaning: Franklin Roosevelt's 1930s programme of economic recovery measures
after cards are shuffled again, a fresh hand is dealt

explanation.surface: A president launches a scheme after changing his cabinet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reshuffle' suggests a cabinet change, but the second sense is cards: once the pack is reshuffled, a fresh distribution of hands comes next.
explanation.definitionFit: Roosevelt's economic recovery programme was a famous presidential policy package.

clue.text: For Romans, that is almost one day every month

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so the final letter of the Latin phrase is dropped

parts.note: id est is Latin, the Romans' tongue, for 'that is'

explanation.surface: The Romans had a particular day each month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' removes the T from ID EST. In the Roman calendar the ides fell on the 13th or 15th of each month.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Roman calendar the ides was a fixed date falling mid-month, every month.

clue.text: Endlessly flourish a peg

indicators.note: something endless has its tail cut off, so the phrase loses its final letter

parts.note: to flourish is to thrive or do well

explanation.surface: Someone waves a peg about with a never-ending flourish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' drops the last L from DO WELL.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowel is a wooden pin used to join pieces of timber, a kind of peg.

clue.text: Part of musical that's particularly fine, for example

definitions.meaning: a set-piece number within a stage show
an especially fine example, one put on display as the best of its kind

explanation.surface: One number in the musical stands out as especially good.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words it is a piece in a show; as one, it is a prize exhibit.
explanation.definitionFit: A showpiece is an outstanding specimen displayed as a model of excellence.

clue.text: Old, as a walrus obviously is

definitions.meaning: a walrus has huge tusks, literally long teeth

explanation.surface: An elderly walrus, as anyone can see.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for elderly comes from horses' gums receding with age; a walrus, with its tusks, is literally so.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means elderly, from the way an ageing horse's gums recede.

clue.text: Press editor in city down under

parts.note: to dun is to press a debtor for payment
taken as written

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor working in an Antipodean city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' looks like journalism, but it is the verb: to press for money owed.
explanation.definitionFit: Dunedin is a city in the South Island of New Zealand, the 'down under' of the clue.

clue.text: Top people booked in this show — how strange

indicators.note: strange means odd or out of order, signalling the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Everyone of note is appearing in this production, oddly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges SHOW and HOW. 'booked' means listed in a book, not reserved for a show.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the annual reference book listing notable and distinguished people.

clue.text: Luggage on flight that's well contained

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: a flight is a set of steps, a single stair being part of it
a case is a suitcase, an item of luggage

explanation.surface: Bags taken on a plane journey are safely stowed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' looks like air travel, but it is a flight of steps; and 'well' is a stairwell, the shaft that encloses steps.
explanation.definitionFit: A staircase sits inside a stairwell, the vertical shaft built to enclose it.

clue.text: Before work, take girl dancing

indicators.note: one piece placed before another comes first in the answer

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
OP is short for opus, Latin for a work

explanation.surface: Ahead of a shift, someone takes a young woman out dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take' is a link. The galop is a lively nineteenth-century ballroom dance, so 'dancing' stands loosely for the dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A galop is a fast ballroom dance in two-four time, a form of dancing.

clue.text: Church that's fine for cardinal

parts.note: i.e., from Latin id est, means 'that is'
F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A church considers a cardinal to be a fine fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cardinal' looks like a churchman, which fits the surface, but here it is the adjective meaning principal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal as an adjective means principal or most important, a synonym.

clue.text: Picture satisfies the photographer, finally, in viewfinder

parts.note: a canvas is a painting, a picture

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of each of the three words before it

explanation.surface: A painting pleases the photographer looking through the camera eyepiece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'viewfinder' is not the camera part: someone who seeks out people's views, as a canvasser polling voters does.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who goes door to door asking people's opinions, literally a seeker of views.

clue.text: Describe food store having eaten there after moving north

parts.note: a deli, short for delicatessen, is a shop selling prepared foods

indicators.note: north is N, and moving it shifts that letter of the word eaten to the front

explanation.surface: Someone describes a food shop where they ate after relocating northwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving north' takes the N of EATEN to the front, giving NEATE; 'having' and 'there' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To delineate is to describe or portray something precisely, a synonym.

clue.text: Considered ready for the post

definitions.meaning: a matter that has been dealt with or tackled
an envelope bearing a destination is ready to be mailed

explanation.surface: Something deemed fit to be mailed.
explanation.walkthrough: One sense is dealing with an issue; the other is an envelope with its destination written on.
explanation.definitionFit: A problem dealt with has been tackled; a letter so marked carries its destination.

clue.text: The old will never raise this alarm

definitions.text: The old will never raise this alarm

parts.words: The old will never raise this alarm
parts.note: the elderly, set in their ways, are never worried by anything old; the alarm in question is a fear of anything novel

explanation.surface: Elderly people will never sound this warning.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is formed from Greek neo-, new, and phobia, fear: it is dread of the unfamiliar, so the old cannot cause it.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a dread of anything new or unfamiliar, from Greek roots for new and fear.

clue.text: Swagger of hired killer holding a duke

indicators.note: one piece holding another wraps around it, so the killer's word surrounds the rest

parts.note: a bravo is a hired assassin or thug

explanation.surface: An assassin swaggers about with a duke in his grip.
explanation.walkthrough: BRAVO is the old word for a hired assassin; A and D go inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravado is a show of boldness intended to impress, a synonym of swagger.

clue.text: For example, a clause in document

definitions.meaning: a is an instance of the indefinite one in grammar
a separate section or provision in a legal text or treaty

explanation.surface: A clause found, say, in a document.
explanation.walkthrough: In grammar the word 'a' is an indefinite article, so it is an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar 'a' and 'the' belong to this word class; also a numbered provision of a treaty.

clue.text: Barrier that gives better security

definitions.meaning: a row of bushes forming a boundary
a gambler covers a wager by betting the other way to limit losses

explanation.surface: A fence that offers a punter some protection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' is one who bets, not 'more good'; hedging a bet protects against loss.
explanation.definitionFit: A row of shrubs forms a boundary; to bet both ways is to protect a wager.

clue.text: Freely available from head librarian

indicators.note: available from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Books may be borrowed freely from the chief librarian.
explanation.walkthrough: AD LIB ends 'head' and starts 'librarian'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ad lib, from Latin ad libitum, means at one's pleasure, without restraint.

clue.text: Scored slowly, and partly followed advice of Polonius?

definitions.meaning: marked in a musical score to be played at a slow tempo
Polonius says 'neither a borrower nor a lender be'; one who lent nothing obeys half of that

explanation.surface: Batting slowly, and taking some of an old courtier's counsel.
explanation.walkthrough: Polonius is the counsellor in Shakespeare's Hamlet. Read as LENT 0, the answer means lent nothing, so half of his advice is kept; 'Scored' suggests cricket but means written in music.
explanation.definitionFit: Lento is a musical direction meaning play slowly.

clue.text: Worker and I joining London publication designed to combat crime

parts.note: a worker ant is the crossword's usual worker
the FT, the Financial Times, is a London newspaper

explanation.surface: A labourer and I join a London newspaper set up to fight crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' and 'joining' are links; THE FT is the Financial Times.
explanation.definitionFit: An anti-theft device is built to prevent stealing, a kind of crime.

clue.text: Cast most of the line

indicators.note: most of a word is all but its final letter

parts.note: a row is a line of things side by side

explanation.surface: Most of the actors are lined up for the cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims THE to TH; 'Cast' suggests actors but means fling.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast is to fling or toss, a synonym.

clue.text: A strain adapted for famous singer

indicators.note: adapted means altered into a new form, signalling the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tune is rearranged for a celebrated vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adapted' rearranges the seven letters of A STRAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank Sinatra was a celebrated American crooner, an example.

clue.text: No beggar will take chore so awful

indicators.note: awful means badly done, signalling the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A down-and-out will take on a dreadful job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' rearranges CHORE SO. The definition draws on the saying 'beggars can't be choosers'.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says beggars can't be picky, so one who can pick is no beggar.

clue.text: Bird that's on board, initially unable to move

definitions.meaning: a black crow-like bird that nests in colonies

definitions.text: on board, initially unable to move
definitions.meaning: a chess piece in the corner, hemmed in at the start of a game

explanation.surface: A bird that has landed on the deck cannot move at first.
explanation.walkthrough: At the start of a chess game the castle sits in the corner, blocked by its own pieces until others move.
explanation.definitionFit: A crow-family bird; also the chess castle, boxed in when play begins.

clue.text: Predict what's to follow, after warning call

indicators.note: one piece placed after another comes later in the answer

parts.note: fore is the golfer's shout warning of a flying ball
a shadow follows its owner, and to shadow is to tail

explanation.surface: Forecasting what will happen once a warning has been sounded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what's to follow' tempts as part of the definition, but it is the wordplay: something that trails behind you.
explanation.definitionFit: To foreshadow is to hint at or presage what is coming, close to predicting.
